text: Attendance and Working Hours Policy The company expects all employees to follow the working hours assigned to their respective roles, departments, or shifts. Employees are responsible for reporting to work on time and completing their assigned working hours on each working day. All employees are required to record their attendance using the attendance system approved by the company. Employees should ensure that their attendance information is recorded accurately and on time. Any issue with the attendance system should be reported to the appropriate manager or HR representative. Employees are expected to be present during their assigned working hours unless they have been approved for leave, work from home, or another authorized arrangement. Employees working in different shifts must follow the start and end times communicated for their assigned shift. Employees are responsible for checking their attendance records and reporting any incorrect or missing information. Employees who arrive after their scheduled start time may be considered late. Repeated late arrivals may require a discussion with the employee's manager and may be reviewed by the HR department. If an employee is unable to report to work because of an unexpected situation, the employee should inform their manager as soon as possible. The employee may also be required to provide the appropriate information or documentation depending on the circumstances. Employees should follow the company's procedures for requesting leave or working from home. Managers are responsible for monitoring attendance within their teams and addressing repeated attendance issues when necessary. Managers may discuss attendance concerns with employees and provide guidance regarding expected working hours and attendance procedures. Employees must not intentionally provide incorrect attendance information or record attendance on behalf of another employee. Any misuse of the attendance system may be reviewed by management or HR. Repeated attendance violations, unauthorized absences, continued late arrivals, or failure to follow assigned working hours may result in appropriate disciplinary action in accordance with company policies. Employees are expected to maintain accurate attendance records and follow all applicable attendance and working-hour procedures. Questions regarding attendance, working hours, leave, or attendance records should be directed to the employee's manager or the HR department.

Employee Benefits Policy The company provides a range of benefits to eligible employees based on applicable company policies and eligibility requirements. Employees should review the benefits available to them and complete any required enrollment process within the specified enrollment period. The benefits offered by the company may include medical insurance, life insurance, paid leave, and wellness programs. The availability of a particular benefit may depend on the employee's eligibility, employment status, and the applicable company rules. Employees who are eligible for medical insurance may receive coverage for services such as hospitalization, medical consultations, and diagnostic services. The exact coverage available to an employee will depend on the applicable insurance plan. Medical insurance may also provide coverage for eligible family members or dependents according to the terms and conditions of the insurance plan. Employee Conduct and Code of Ethics The company expects all employees to maintain professional, respectful, and ethical behavior while performing their responsibilities. Employees are expected to follow company policies, procedures, and applicable ethical standards. Employees should treat colleagues, managers, customers, business partners, and other individuals with respect and professionalism. All employees are expected to act with honesty, integrity, and fairness in their day-to-day activities. Employees must understand and follow the standards of behavior expected in the workplace. Harassment, discrimination, fraud, theft, violence, or any other inappropriate behavior is not acceptable and may be subject to appropriate action under company policies. Employees are responsible for protecting company information and maintaining the confidentiality of information they receive as part of their work. Confidential company information must not be shared, disclosed, or used without proper authorization. Employees should report workplace concerns through the appropriate company channels.
